history.summary: The Sri Jagannath Mandir at Gayatri Nagar (Avanti Vihar / Shankar Nagar, pin 492007) was founded in 2000, the year Chhattisgarh was formed, and completed in 2003, according to the temple committee's founder president. The neem-wood idols of Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra were brought from Odisha and consecrated by acharyas from the Puri temple; vestments and jewelry for Rath Yatra are ordered from Puri and the deity is adorned on Puri lines. It is reported as the only temple in Chhattisgarh where the Rath Yatra is inaugurated by the state head performing the Chhera-Pahra ritual (sweeping the route with a gold broom), with three chariots including Nandi Ghosh and Devdalan. The complex, a replica of the Puri temple, also houses small shrines of Rama, Shiva, Mangala, Ganesha, Hanuman and Surya, and a stone Gita-upadesha tableau (Krishna as charioteer) at the main gate. CONFLICT (verify): velpu.com claims a Raipur Jagannath temple 'built in 1860' — this likely refers to a different/older shrine; the documented Gayatri Nagar temple is the 2000-2003 one.

name: Sri Jagannath Mandir, Raipur
town_description: Raipur is the capital of Chhattisgarh (since the state's formation in 2000) and its largest city, a major commercial and industrial hub of central India known for steel plants and rice milling. The old city around Purani Basti and the Kharun river preserves its pre-modern core, while newer areas like VIP Road and Naya Raipur reflect rapid recent growth. It is well connected by rail and air and serves as the gateway to Chhattisgarh's temples and national parks.

travel.road: Gayatri Nagar / Avanti Vihar, near Shankar Nagar; reachable by auto/taxi via city roads

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; Rath Yatra (June-July) is the major festival
